items.title: tiny-js stays a dependency-free scripting engine for its hosts while it moves to Rust

fields.summary: Applications that embed tiny-js for simple scripting and settings (P1, P2) keep the same behaviour while the engine is rebuilt in Rust.

items.title: Characterise the C++ interpreter before changing it

fields.summary: Capture what the C++ build does today, as golden outputs, so every later change is measured against it.

items.title: Rebuild the interpreter in Rust behind the same interfaces

fields.summary: Port the values, parser, built-ins, and embedding API to Rust, one step at a time, each proved against the golden outputs.

items.title: Golden outputs of the C++ build

fields.summary: The 38 test scripts and the command-line runner's output and errors, captured from the C++ build at a pinned commit.
fields.problem: There is no product documentation, so the only definition of correct behaviour is what the C++ build does (E5, E6, E11).
fields.scope: In: run_tests per script (G1), the command-line runner's stdout on each script (G2), its error output (G3). Out: the *.42.js tests and tests/42tests, which run_tests never runs (E11); Math.rand sequences (E16).

items.title: Capture pass or fail of the 38 test scripts from the C++ build

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want each test script's pass or fail captured from the C++ build, so that the Rust build is held to the same results.
fields.completion_goal: 1. [api-trace] state: run_tests built with make from commit 8214477 and the cases file for case set G1; expected: aayu survey --golden writes 38 cases, each with exit code 0, and a manifest with the build's SHA-256
fields.scenario: Build with make, then run the G1 capture once.
fields.environment: Linux, g++ and make, the repository's tests/ only

items.title: Capture the command-line runner's output and errors

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want the command-line runner's output on every test script and on script errors captured, so that what a person sees stays the same.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: Script built with make from commit 8214477 and case set G2 (37 scripts, test019 excluded for Math.rand); expected: aayu survey --golden captures each case's stdout and exit code 0
2. [api-trace] state: case set G3, a syntax error and a call of an undefined function; expected: the capture records an ERROR line with line and column on stdout and exit code 1
fields.scenario: Build with make, then run the G2 and G3 capture once.
fields.environment: Linux, g++ and make, the repository's tests/ only

fields.summary: The lexer, values, and recursive-descent parser in Rust, running the same scripts with the same results.
fields.problem: The C++ engine manages memory by reference counting that leaks cycles (E4), keeps children in linked lists (E3), and leaks every caught error (E15).
fields.scope: In: lexer, values, parser, execution, error messages with positions (R1). Out: new language features and fixes to the known gaps until Q2 is answered.

items.title: Port the lexer and value model to Rust

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want the lexer and values in Rust with ownership instead of manual reference counts, so that cycles no longer leak.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the Rust test runner built from this branch and case set G1; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference for every G1 case whose script uses only literals, variables, and objects
2. [api-trace] state: a script that sets a.foo = a, run 10,000 times in one process; expected: resident memory after the last run is within 5% of after the first
fields.scenario: Replay G1, then run the cycle script in a loop.

items.title: Port the parser and execution to Rust

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want the parser and execution in Rust, so that every script runs as it did in C++.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the Rust test runner and case set G1; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference
2. [api-trace] state: the Rust command-line runner and case sets G2 and G3; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference, including the ERROR line's line and column
fields.scenario: Replay the three case sets on the Rust build.

items.title: Built-in and Math libraries in Rust

fields.summary: The string, array, integer, object, JSON, exec, eval, and Math built-ins in Rust.
fields.problem: The built-ins are C++ callbacks registered by name (C6); the command-line runner registers only half of them (E7).
fields.scope: In: every function registered today, with the same names and signatures. Out: registering Math in the command-line runner, unless Q4 says the runner is part of the product; reproducing Math.rand's sequence (Q5).

items.title: Port the built-in and Math functions to Rust

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want every built-in function in Rust under the same name, so that scripts that call them keep working.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the Rust test runner and case set G1; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference
2. [api-trace] state: the Rust command-line runner and case set G2; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference
3. [api-trace] state: Math.randInt(1,6) called 1,000 times; expected: every value is an integer from 1 to 6
fields.scenario: Replay G1 and G2, then call randInt in a loop.

fields.summary: Hosts create an interpreter, register native functions, execute and evaluate script, and read or set variables, from Rust and through a C ABI.
fields.problem: Hosts call the C++ classes directly today (E1); a Rust engine needs an interface they can switch to.
fields.scope: In: execute, evaluate, addNative, getVariable, setVariable as a Rust crate and a C ABI. Out: the CScriptVar class API, until Q1 says hosts use it.

items.title: Ship the Rust crate and C ABI, then retire the C++ build

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want hosts to embed the Rust engine through the same five calls, so that the C++ build can go.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: a C host program that registers print through the C ABI and executes tests/test001.js; expected: it prints the same output as the golden G2 case for test001 and exits 0
2. [api-trace] state: the Rust build and case sets G1, G2, and G3; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference in any of them
fields.scenario: Build the C host against the ABI, then replay the three case sets.
fields.environment: Linux, cargo, cc, the repository's tests/

items.title: The known-issue list says postfix ++ is broken, but the code fixed it in 0.31

fields.summary: The NOTE block at the top of TinyJS.cpp lists a bug the version history says was fixed and the code no longer has.
fields.reproduce: Run Script on: var a=1; var b=a++; print(b);
fields.expected: The NOTE block lists only issues that still occur.
fields.actual: It prints 1 (the previous value, which is correct), while TinyJS.cpp:111 says the current value is returned.
fields.completion_goal: 1. [api-trace] state: TinyJS.cpp after the fix; expected: the NOTE block no longer lists the postfix increment, and aayu survey --parity on case set G1 reports no difference
fields.measure: stale entries in the NOTE block
fields.scenario: Read the NOTE block against the golden outputs.

items.title: run_tests overflows a 64-byte buffer for a long test path

fields.summary: A failing test whose path is longer than 55 characters overflows the buffer that holds its .fail.js name.
fields.reproduce: Copy a failing test to a path of 60 characters and run run_tests on it.
fields.expected: The runner writes <path>.fail.js and reports FAIL.
fields.actual: sprintf writes past the 64-byte stack buffer fn (run_tests.cpp:228-229).
fields.completion_goal: 1. [api-trace] state: run_tests built with -fsanitize=address and a failing test at a 60-character path; expected: FAIL is printed, the .fail.js file is written, and the sanitizer reports nothing
fields.scenario: Run the long-path failing test under AddressSanitizer.

items.title: Every caught script error leaks its exception object

fields.summary: Errors are thrown as heap pointers and the command-line runner never deletes them.
fields.reproduce: Run Script interactively and type a line with a syntax error 1,000 times.
fields.actual: Each error allocates a CScriptException that is never freed (TinyJS.cpp:1344, Script.cpp:103-105).
fields.completion_goal: 1. [api-trace] state: Script under valgrind fed 100 lines with a syntax error; expected: valgrind reports 0 bytes definitely lost, and aayu survey --parity on case set G3 reports no difference
fields.scenario: Feed the error lines on stdin under valgrind.

open_questions: Q1 (open): which hosts embed tiny-js and through which API; decides the C ABI's scope in rust-api-and-abi
Q2 (open): keep or correct the known gaps (Array(5), length, prefix ++); no item fixes them until answered
Q3 (open): untrusted scripts; an execution-limit Story waits for the answer
Q4 (open): is the command-line runner part of the product
